## A split model's experts in RAM sized from the machine; the website benchmark goes on after a failed size

- **The RAM tier of a model split over several GPUs is sized from its parts** (manoreken2, PR #100): each GPU keeps up to its own share of the experts in RAM, and on Windows up to the budget divided by the GPUs, less what is mapped already and 8 GiB, divided by the GPUs again (each GPU counts the shared pinned memory against Windows' budget in full). The fixed caps of 32 GiB a GPU and 128 GiB in all are gone on Windows: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash Q8_K_XL over 4 Pro B60s goes from 32 to ~46 GiB a GPU, where 47 took an 8K prompt from 63.5 to 142.3 tok/s. Linux keeps its caps until a run there measures the limit. One start line names the parts.
- **`bench/website_bench` keeps going after a size fails** (#99): the size is recorded as failed, the model's larger sizes skipped, and the generation modes and the KL still run; a failed KL run says why. Each size records how much of the weights sat in host RAM.

**Please test on your machine** (paste the output into the issue):

Several GPUs on Windows (#100), with your usual model and command, and no `ARC_XRAM_GB`:

```
serverz -m <model> --gpus 4 --ctx auto
```

Look for the line "experts read from the SSD are also kept in RAM, up to ... GiB (...)" and post it with your prompt speed.

An Arc A380 or another small card (#99): the website benchmark as before:

```
bash bench/website_bench.sh --models <Qwen3.5-4B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf>
```
